items.title: NASA's Artemis II moon mission set to launch Wednesday

featured_image.name: Victor Glover Artemis II Crew Announcement Resource Reel

items.description: NASA is hours away from launching the first crewed mission to the moon in more than half a century, with Navy Captain Victor Glover at the controls. The Artemis II mission is scheduled to lift off on Wednesday, April 1, at 6:24 p.m. EDT from Launch Complex 39B at Kennedy Space Center in Florida, sending four astronauts on an approximately 10-day journey around the moon and back.[1][2]

items.title: Trump warns European allies after Italy, France block US military access

featured_image.name: Trump lashes out at UK and France, telling allies 'the U.S.A. won't be there to help you anymore'

items.description: A widening rift between the United States and its European allies deepened on Tuesday as Italy and France took steps to block American military operations from their territory, prompting President Donald Trump to warn that "the USA won't be there to help you anymore." The escalating dispute over European involvement in the month-old US-Israeli military campaign against Iran is straining the NATO alliance while a parallel energy crisis rattles the continent's economy.

items.title: China verifies Mach 6 engine prototype after 30 years

featured_image.name: China's hypersonic jet shatters Mach 6.5 speed in Gobi desert test

items.description: Chinese researchers have completed and experimentally verified a prototype of a novel air-breathing propulsion system that can accelerate from a dead stop to more than six times the speed of sound, according to a report by the South China Morning Post on Sunday. The engine, called the "contra-rotary ramjet," represents over three decades of development and could reshape the design of future fighter jets and hypersonic missiles.[1][2][3]

items.title: Fourth Greek tanker crosses Hormuz despite Iran blockade

featured_image.name: Oil tanker transits Hormuz in rare voyage after Iran war disruption

items.description:
The Greek-controlled Suezmax tanker Pola has successfully crossed the Strait of Hormuz, becoming the fourth vessel managed by Athens-based Dynacom Tankers Management Ltd. to navigate the chokepoint since the US and Israel launched military strikes against Iran on February 28, according to Bloomberg.[1]

The Pola switched off its Automatic Identification System in the Persian Gulf on March 10 and reappeared on Monday in the eastern Indian Ocean near Indonesia's Sumatra island, vessel tracking data compiled by Bloomberg showed. The tanker, laden with roughly 1 million barrels of crude, is en route to Thailand, according to intelligence firm Kpler.[1]

items.title: King Charles confirms first US state visit as monarch

featured_image.name: King Charles to address Congress in historic first state ... - Fox News

items.description:
Buckingham Palace announced on Tuesday that King Charles III and Queen Camilla will undertake a state visit to the United States in late April, marking the first trip to America by a British monarch since Queen Elizabeth II's visit in 2007.[1][2]

The visit, made at the invitation of President Donald Trump and on the advice of the British government, will celebrate the 250th anniversary of American independence — a milestone with particular resonance given that the U.S. declared independence during the reign of Charles's ancestor King George III.[2]

items.title: U.S., Israel strike Isfahan and Tehran on Day 32 of Iran war

featured_image.name: Pakistan says it will host US-Iran talks after diplomats ... - AP News

items.description: As the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran entered its 32nd day on Tuesday, powerful explosions rocked both Tehran and the central city of Isfahan in what appeared to be some of the most intense aerial bombardments since hostilities began on February 28. The escalation came alongside fresh Iranian retaliatory strikes across the region and a parallel diplomatic push led by Pakistan to bring Washington and Tehran to the negotiating table.[1][2]

items.title: Trump tells allies to 'take' Strait of Hormuz themselves

featured_image.name: Trump criticizes allies who aren't helping secure the Strait of Hormuz

items.description:
President Donald Trump escalated his pressure on reluctant allies on Tuesday, posting on Truth Social that countries struggling with jet fuel shortages caused by Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz should either purchase American oil or seize control of the waterway themselves.

"All of those countries that can't get jet fuel because of the Strait of Hormuz, like the United Kingdom, which refused to get involved in the decapitation of Iran, I have a suggestion for you: Number 1, buy from the US, we have plenty, and Number 2, build up some delayed courage, go to the Strait, and just TAKE IT," Trump wrote, singling out nations that declined to join U.S. strikes against Iran. He added that the United States "won't be there to help you anymore" and that allies would need to learn "how to fight for yourself".[1][2][3]
